dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product has views whose content arrives after the view does — a list fetched after its page opened, a person's details, an article — and already knows the shape of what is coming. It holds that shape in the place while it waits, in one quiet manner everywhere, so that nothing moves when the content arrives; it decides once how quiet the shapes are, how they are rounded, whether and how they stir, and how long a wait lasts before they are shown at all.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a skeleton reads: the space between placeholders that stand one under another; a placeholder's fill; its corners as a line of text, as a block and as a circle; how much of the last of several lines is drawn; how far the fill dims as it stirs, how it stirs (a pulse, a wave or not at all), how long one dimming takes and on which curve; and the wait before the skeleton is shown.
rules: Use a skeleton where content of a known shape will fill a region of a view and the wait is long enough to be seen: the first load of a list, a card, an article, a person's details. Give it placeholders in the shape and the size of what is coming, so that nothing moves when it arrives.

Do not use it for a short wait inside a control, a row or a status line, or for an action under way (saving, sending): that is a loading indicator. Do not use it for a task whose progress can be measured or that takes many seconds: that is a progress indicator.
Do not use it where nothing will come: that is an empty state. Replace the skeleton with the content, with an empty state, or with a callout of the error status — never leave it standing.

One skeleton for one wait: put every placeholder of a region in one skeleton and give it a label (what is loading), so that the wait is said once. Where a loading indicator or a status text already says the same wait, set decorative.
Insert the skeleton when the wait starts and remove it when the content arrives: the show delay counts from its insertion, so a wait shorter than the delay shows nothing and the box is still held.
A text placeholder takes the text style of where it stands: place it where the text will be, as the text will be placed, and its lines are exactly the lines the text will take.
Never put content a person should read or use inside a skeleton: everything inside is kept from input and from assistive technology.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw grey boxes by hand.

gap.$description: The space between two placeholders that stand one under another directly in the skeleton. Placeholders inside a layout of the product's own are spaced by that layout. The lines of one text placeholder have no gap: they are the line boxes of its text style.

color.$description: A placeholder's fill: the low-emphasis fill a track has, quiet enough that a view full of placeholders is not louder than the content that replaces them. Decorative: the wait is said by the skeleton's label, not by this color.

shape.$description: A placeholder's corners, per shape, never larger than half its smaller side.

text.$description: The corners of each line of a text placeholder: barely eased, as a run of letters has no corners of its own.

block.$description: The corners of a block: the corners a card and a picture in content have in the default system.

circle.$description: The corners of a circle: the whole of them.

last-line-inline-size.$description: How much of the last line of a text placeholder of two or more lines is drawn, as a fraction of the placeholder's inline size, from the start edge: a paragraph seldom ends at the edge, and a ragged end is what makes a stack of bars read as text. 1 draws every line whole.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A fraction of the placeholder's own inline size, not a distance; no dial moves it.

dim-opacity.$description: The opacity a placeholder's fill falls to at the low point of a pulse or in the trough of a wave, as a fraction of its resting opacity. 1 leaves the fill still under either manner.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A fraction of the fill's own opacity; no dial moves it, and the motion dial scales durations, not depths.

animation.$description: How a shown skeleton stirs, so that it reads as waiting and not as broken. pulse: every placeholder's fill dims and returns, all of them together. wave: the same dimming passes through the skeleton from its start edge to its end edge, as one band across all of its placeholders. none: the placeholders are still. Under reduced motion every manner is drawn as none. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A choice of kind; no dial scales it.

dim-duration.$description: How long the fill takes to fall from its resting opacity to its dim opacity; the way back takes as long, so one whole pulse, and one whole wave across the skeleton, is twice this.

dim-easing.$description: The curve of the fall and of the way back.

show-delay.$description: How long the skeleton waits, from the moment it is inserted, before it is drawn and exposed to assistive technology, so that a wait shorter than this shows the place blank instead of shapes that flash. Its box is kept during the wait.
